topics.label: Lecture framing and the cancer hallmarks framework
topics.groupedBecause: This opening establishes the lecture’s learning outcomes and introduces cancer hallmarks as the framework for interpreting tumor progression.

topics.label: Deregulated extracellular signaling and growth control
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signaling pathways allow cancer cells to sustain proliferation and survival despite normal growth controls.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how disrupted cell differentiation shapes cancer phenotypes in hematological and intestinal tissues.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how disruption of p53 signaling and the balance of mitochondrial apoptotic regulators enables cancer cells to evade death.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance and tumor cell immortalization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how telomere shortening limits normal cell proliferation and how increased telomerase expression lets cancer cells bypass that limit.

topics.label: p53-mediated genome protection and growth-control recap
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consolidate the mechanisms that normally safeguard growth control and whose disruption generates cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how altered metabolism characterizes cancer cells and can reinforce the molecular changes driving tumor development.

topics.label: Angiogenesis and vascular support for tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains why tumor growth requires an angiogenic switch that supplies oxygen and nutrients through new vasculature.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination and successful secondary growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells reach distant sites and what determines whether their dissemination produces detectable metastases.

topics.label: Closing synthesis and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the shared hallmarks reached through diverse cancer trajectories, recommends further reading, and concludes the lecture.
